sources: AllMusic 4.5/5 (John Young) | WQXR top 10 essential Glass recordings | The Quietus 30th-anniversary feature | commercial breakthrough, gave Glass name recognition | NYT later called it a footnote in his catalogue | mainstream: composer-crafted, deliberately shorter accessible pop-oriented pieces for a general audience

BBC Music Magazine / classical-music.com review: 'a musical masterpiece' | Tom Johnson, Village Voice (1974): 'a major accomplishment' | Classical Voice North America (John Rockwell, 2024): a 'watershed', marked his transition | philipglass.com (Tim Page): 'the longest and most ambitious concert piece for the Philip Glass Ensemble' | mainstream: four-hour ensemble cycle, rarely performed

Routledge, Einstein on the Beach: Opera beyond Drama (Novak & Richardson, 2019): 'the landmark opera', 'widely acknowledged as a profoundly significant moment in the history of opera', polarized reactions at early performances | NPR (Mark Mobley, 2012): 'the groundbreaking minimalist opera on a maximal scale' | FACT (2012): 'Glass's first and best opera' | NYT (Clive Barnes, 1976, quoted by NPR 2013): 'bizarre, occasionally boring, yet always intermittently beautiful' | mainstream: plotless 4.5-hour avant-garde opera

FACT (2012): among '10 essential works' of Glass, 'cumulative, mathematical intensity' | NPR (Jacob Ganz, 2012, interview with The Fader's Matthew Schnipper): heard at fashion shows, live screenings draw every kind of audience | WNYC New Sounds (2020): 'propulsive score' | mainstream: film score with a broad audience, composer-led
